padroes.========================================:
====================================================================
  NOTES
====================================================================

- "native +{0} bonus" is the bonus the game itself already switched on
  when every piece was +{1} or higher. It still applies and stacks with
  the enchant ladder explained at the start.

- "attributes" are the STR/DEX/CON/INT/WIT/MEN points the set gives or
  takes away.

- "with shield" only applies if the set's shield is equipped.

- The three base Dynasty tier-{2} sets (Jewel Leather, Platinum Plate
  and Silver Satin, the ones WITHOUT a class name) had no set at all in
  the original game - not even on the official one. They were created
  here with the bonus of the base Dynasty of the same type.

- The enchant bonus is only recalculated when the piece is re-equipped or at login. Enchanting a piece already worn does not
  update it on the spot.

- The Native (No Grade) set gives no stat: it turns the character into
  a native. The DEX +{3} was added by us.

- The "Clan Oath" and "Shadow Item: Clan Oath" sets share the same
  skill: their bonus is always identical, by the game's own design.

THE SKILL LEVEL COMES FROM THE STONE LEVEL. For the {3} skills that
have {4} levels:

   stone {5} -> lv {6}        stone {7} -> lv  {8}
   stone {9} -> lv {10}        stone {11} -> lv  {12}
   stone {13} -> lv {14}        stone {15} -> lv  {16}

The ones with fewer levels saturate earlier; each one's list says

the common box, {26}% is the rare one (see Part {27}).

THE PASSIVES THAT SAY "Chance: ... when receiving damage" have a chance
of their own, and it appears in brackets on each level's line.

padroes.O BÔNUS DE ENCANTAMENTO DEPENDIA DA ORDE:
THE ENCHANT BONUS DEPENDED ON THE ORDER YOU PUT THE PIECES ON   ({0}/{1}/{2})

  SERIOUS BUG, found because the owner complained that a full HEAVY +{3}
  set showed no passive at all. It applied to ALL THREE types.

  WHAT WAS HAPPENING. The LightSetEnchant script has to be told when the
  player equips or removes a piece, and in the engine that notice is
  registered PER ITEM TEMPLATE. The script only registered the notice on
  pieces whose armor_type was LIGHT, HEAVY or MAGIC.

  And there is the trap: in High Five ONLY THE CHEST AND THE LEGS declare
  armor_type. Helmet, gloves and boots declare nothing - they stay NONE.
  So the script was BLIND to three of the set's five pieces.

  CONSEQUENCE: the bonus only appeared by ACCIDENT, when the chest (or the
  legs) was the LAST piece to go on. Anyone who put the chest on first and
  closed with the helmet got no bonus at all, with the full set showing on
  screen. And anyone who took the helmet off still had the bonus running.

  HOW IT WAS PROVEN, and not deduced: the server log said

     [LightSetEnchant] Miquerinos: set do peito {4} incompleto

  while the database showed the five correct pieces of set {5} equipped,
  all +{6}. Both can only be true at the same time if the sum was never
  recomputed after the last piece - and the last log line was from two
  minutes BEFORE the last equip. In the same log, the LIGHT set had worked
  fifteen minutes earlier, precisely because there the chest was the last
  piece.

  THE FIX: the filter now goes by SLOT (chest, legs, head, gloves, feet
  and full_armor) instead of by armour type. Compiled clean against the jar
  in use before saving. On server start-up, the line
  "[LightSetEnchant] listeners registrados em N templates de armadura"
  has to show an N far HIGHER than before.

  AS A BONUS, the log became useful: when the set is incomplete it now
  lists the five pieces and says which one failed. Before it only said
  "incompleto" and you had to go and query the database to find out why.

  LIMITATION THAT REMAINS: there is no enchant event in the engine.
  Enchanting a piece that is ALREADY equipped does not recalculate - only
  re-equipping or relogging does.
padroes.O BÔNUS PvP DO VESPER NOBLE LEATHER ANUN:
THE VESPER NOBLE LEATHER PvP BONUS ADVERTISED THE WRONG EFFECT   ({0}/{1}/{2})

  Owner's complaint: the Vesper Noble Leather Breastplate {PvP} said
  "Decreases damage received during PvP, and all speeds of the attacker
  decrease at a certain rate" - which is the HEAVY set bonus.

  THE SERVER WAS NEVER WRONG. I swept the {3} {PvP} sets,
  cross-checking the chest's armor_type against the trigger the set grants:

     HEAVY  ->  {4}  PvP Armor - Speed Down
     LIGHT  ->  {5}  PvP Armor - Mirage        (takes the target off its target)
     MAGIC  ->  {6}  PvP Armor - Critical Down

  All {7} match. The {8} Vesper Noble Light Armor Set for Adults already
  granted {9} Mirage. The only thing lying was the client TEXT.

  Fixed in itemname-e.dat, in both variants (chests {10} and
  {11}), copying the wording of its Vesper Leather {PvP} sibling ({12}),
  which describes this very trigger:

     "Decreases damage received during PvP, and improves the chance to
      blow away a target's target when being attacked, and the cloak
      slot opens."

  THREE MORE TYPOS in the same family, found in the sweep:

     {13} / {14}   "decrease all a certain rate"  ->  "at"
     {15} / {16}   "...attacked.; and the cloak"  ->  ", and the cloak"
     {17} / {18}   "...attacked.; and the cloak"  ->  ", and the cloak"

  What was deliberately NOT touched: there are {19} different wordings of
  the PvP bonus across the {20} sets - one per era (Dynasty writes
  "cancel opponent's target", Vesper writes "blow away a target's
  target"). The other {21} describe the correct effect for their own type.
  Different wording for the same effect is not a defect, and standardising
  it would erase the difference between eras. After the fix the sweep closes
  at {22} correct / {23} wrong.

padroes.Todo augment tem DUAS metades, sorteadas:
Every augment has TWO halves, rolled separately:

  HALF {0}   always a STAT bonus. Never fails.
  HALF {1}   {2}% of the time a SECOND stat bonus,
           {3}% of the time a SKILL.

What controls what:

  the stone LEVEL ({4}, {5} ... {6})
      controls the VALUE of the stats and the LEVEL of the skill;
  the stone GRADE (common, Mid, High, Top)
      controls only the value of HALF {7}. The better the grade,
      the bigger the number. Measured stat by stat:

        Mid {8}x to {9}x, High {10}x to {11}x, Top {12}x to {13}x

      (compared with the common stone of the SAME level)

THREE THINGS THAT USUALLY COME AS A SURPRISE:

  {14}) THE STONE GRADE DOES NOT CHANGE THE CHANCE OF A SKILL. Common,
     Mid, High and Top all have the same {15}%. Going up a grade buys
     a bigger stat, not a better chance of a skill.
     (config/Player.ini: the four
      RetailLikeAugmentation...Chance lines are all at {16}.)

  {17}) THE GRADE DOES NOT CHANGE HALF {18} EITHER. Checked across the {19}
     stones: the four stones of one and the same level reach
     exactly the same list in half {20}.

  {21}) A {22} AND A {23} STONE GIVE THE SAME VALUE AS A {24} ONE. The last
     value band in the file is the {25} one, and the {26} and
     {27} stones point to it.

A PHYSICAL weapon and a MAGICAL weapon have separate lists in the file, but
the stats and the values are the same, and the skills are the same
{28}. This document applies to both.
